text:
maria: Quick sweep results across us-west1 / eu-west1 / ap-southeast1 for L4 / T4 / A10G — embeddings + small-chat. overview + charts: https://redwood.internal/bench/1925/gpu-sweep.png :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ajay: grabbing raw CSVs, will paste numbers in a sec

jen: TL;DR (short):
- embeddings (small queries ~128 tokens): L4 p50=18ms, p95=42ms, throughput=750 qps, est cost ~$0.12 / 1M queries.
- embeddings T4 p50=28ms, p95=68ms, throughput=480 qps, est cost ~$0.08 / 1M queries (cheaper infra but slower).
- embeddings A10G p50=12ms, p95=26ms, throughput=1200 qps, est cost ~$0.20 / 1M queries.

- small-chat (avg resp ~512 tokens): L4 p50=65ms, p95=210ms, tps=120, cost ~$0.15 / 1M tokens.
- small-chat T4 p50=95ms, p95=330ms, tps=70, cost ~$0.11 / 1M tokens.
- small-chat A10G p50=40ms, p95=120ms, tps=220, cost ~$0.30 / 1M tokens.

kai: Kernel notes: L4 runs best with `flash_attn_v2` + `sliced_kv` (keeps memory footprint low). T4 needed `attention_fallback` for 512+ tokens (we saw soft failures). A10G benefits from `mma` kernels and larger smem paths.

bench-bot: Quant sweep summary (auto): `fp16` vs `int8_gptq` vs `groupwise_int8`
- int8_gptq: mem ~2.7x reduction, latency ~0.9x, embedding cosine drift ~0.8% (avg).
- groupwise_int8: similar mem, slightly better embedding quality (0.4% drift) but slower than gptq on A10G.

ajay: regional differences: eu-west1 p50 +7-9ms vs us-west1 (host packing), ap-southeast1 had heavier T4 p95 tails due to PCIe jitter and shared NIC. We profiled p95 spikes to PCIe stalls on older T4 images.

maria: early recommendation:
- embeddings: L4 is the sweet-spot for cost-sensitive production (good throughput + lower infra $/q).
- high-req low-latency SLOs: A10G (pay more for latency headroom).
- T4: only for spot/low-commit burst or legacy SKU constraints — watch memory fragmentation.

maria: config snippet we used for the runs:
```
model: rwd/llama-embed-13b
quant: int8_gptq
kernels: [flash_attn_v2, sliced_kv]
batching: {max_tokens: 4096, max_batch: 256}
autoscale: {min:1, max:8}
```

kai: note: on T4 we hit OOM with `max_batch=256` for chat. dropping to 128 fixed it — fragmentation issue. Also observed that `prefetch_kv=2` reduced tail by ~15% on A10G.

jen: quality regression check: int8_gptq produced a handful of embedding outliers for rare tokens (detected via cosine < 0.6), tagging those prompts in the eval suite. overall pass rate 99.2% vs fp16 baseline.

ajay: action items: 1) run 24h A10G tail-run in eu-west1 (scheduled now, ETA ~24h) 2) run groupwise-quant on L4 for small-chat (jen) 3) update Console cost-model with these numbers (ajay)

maria: noted. also we'll add kernel fallback rules: prefer `flash_attn_v2` on L4/A10G, enable `attention_fallback` only on T4 and limit batch sizes.

bench-bot: logs uploaded: https://redwood.internal/bench/1925/logs.zip (contains raw p50/p95 CSVs, kernel traces)

kai: small tip: if you see T4 p95 spikes, check `nvidia-smi topo -m` and PCIe link speed, and try `--cgroup-memory-swap` tweaks; helped us in apac.

maria: thanks — we'll fold this into model bring-up doc and the onboarding checklist. ping me if anyone wants the raw experiment Jupyter. :thumbsup:
